newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks edge down, market seen stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks edge down, market seen stagnant.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly lower on Friday and traders predicted the market would stagnate as most investors exhausted their funds in December.
"I expect no significant changes in prices next week," said Ratko Bubalo of Eastbrokers.
But he added that a growing number of small investors would become active in a longer run, seeing good profits in stocks as banks further trim interest rates on savings.
Six of 11 active issues were down on Friday, three rose and two stayed flat. Volume rose to 14,025 shares, but turnover shrank to 5.3 million kuna from 7.8 million on Thursday.

Blue chip drugs firm Pliva was the biggest gainer, up 35 kuna up to 450 -- a new record. It was also most actively traded with 8,257 units sold. Its GDRs hit a $16.56 high on the London Stock Exchange earlier in the day.
The other fully-listed issue, Zagrebacka Banka, was also on the gaining streak, adding 92 kuna to 1,300 on a small volume of three shares.
Biggest loser, confectioner Kras, dropped 40 kuna to 500 on volume of 619 units. Bubalo described the stock as "very interesting."
"The dip occurred because many small shareholders were ready to sell. It is usual for January when everyone pays their bills," he added.
Among the losers was also hotelier Suncani Hvar, four kuna down to 60, with 1,021 units sold and Jadranturist which lost 15 kuna to 300 on volume of 155.
